subject: Request: Force-model pin + region restriction for Helios PoC — exception review
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Force-model pin + region restriction for Helios PoC — exception review

Team —

Helios (PoC for their clinical notes workflow) just asked us to lock two things for their initial rollout:

- Pin the service to redwood-llama-2-13b-q4f (no automatic fallback to other families).
- Serve traffic only from us-west-2 (they need region pinning for data residency and approvals).

They claim their regulator requires a consistent model artifact and a single geographic enclave for inference for the PoC window. Sales flagged this as a hard requirement; they will walk away if we can’t guarantee identical model + region.

Questions / asks:
- Hannah: what are the runtime risks (latency SLO, capacity pressure) for removing fallback and enforcing a single-region lock?
- Jonas: product/roadmap implications — can we make this a temporary exception (90d) and what rollout controls do you want?
- Karthik: I need a short sales-friendly summary we can share with the customer showing mitigations and timeline.

Attached: SLA-exception-form.pdf and a rough network-topology.png from the Helios security team.

Goal: decide whether we can approve an exception and, if yes, what operational guardrails we require (dedicated pool, canary, documented rollback).

—Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Force-model pin + region restriction for Helios PoC — exception review

Marissa —

Thanks for the heads up. High-level technical concerns:

1) No-fallback risk: if the 13b model hits OOMs or kernel regressions under peak load we have no automatic degraded path. That increases P1 risk and potentially increases mean-time-to-recovery.
2) Single-region lock: us-west-2 is fine but it concentrates load; without capacity reservation it will compete with other workloads.
3) Latency SLO: 13b quantized in a dedicated pool can meet 150-200ms per-token for typical sequences, but will need tuned batching; unpredictable seq lengths (clinical notes) could spike.

Mitigations I recommend:
- Dedicated GPU reserve (small pool, 2–4 GPUs depending on traffic projection) for the PoC window.
- Emergency fallback mode: an operator-triggered fallback to a smaller 7b family only after human approval (no automatic fallback).
- Enhanced monitoring + synthetic prompts for quality drift and latency.

I attached a short ops note with estimated GPU counts and a runbook snippet.

If the ask is to ban *any* fallback with no operator override, we should flag Legal and Security — that substantially raises our operational exposure.

—Hannah
Eng Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Force-model pin + region restriction for Helios PoC — exception review

Thanks — aligned with Hannah. Product take: we can treat this as a timeboxed commercial exception with the following non-negotiables: 

- The customer signs a routing/model amendment (DocuSign) accepting reduced resiliency guarantees if they block fallback.
- We require a dedicated pool provisioned for the PoC (billing premium applies).
- We maintain an operator-only emergency fallback to a smaller family; it will be documented in the amendment as a last-resort incident mitigation (Helios must acknowledge possible degraded outputs).
- Canary rollout: start at 5% traffic for 7 days, performance verification, then ramp.

Operational POC checklist I propose:
- Legal: amendment draft (Karthik / Lauren)
- Security: confirm network/topology constraints (Marissa)
- Infra: reserve capacity and pre-warm KV caches (Hannah)

If everyone agrees, we should push the amendment to Helios and offer a one-time onboarding credit to cover extra infra costs. I'll add this to the roadmap as a temporary supported pattern (label: "customer-exception:forced-pin"). Link to the internal RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-helix-routing-rfc

—Jonas
Sr Product Manager
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: ops@helioshealth.com, legal@helioshealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Force-model pin + region restriction for Helios PoC — amendment and next steps

Hi Helios team —

Thanks again for the call. Per our discussion, Redwood can support:

- Model pin: redwood-llama-2-13b-q4f (no automatic fallback).
- Region lock: us-west-2 only for inference.
- Operational guardrails: dedicated capacity and an operator-only emergency fallback to a smaller model family.

Next steps:
- We've prepared an amendment that documents the resiliency tradeoffs and the dedicated capacity terms (DocuSign link below). Please review and sign if acceptable.
- We’ll provision the dedicated pool after we receive the signed amendment (typical provisioning 48–72 hours).

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/helios/HLL-2026-0342

To show good faith, we're offering a one-time onboarding credit to offset infra provisioning while you ramp. If you prefer an automatic fallback instead of the operator-only flow, we can discuss that but it will require an updated security attestation.

Thanks — please let us know by EOD next week so we can lock timelines.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: amendment_preview.pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 June 2026 17:06:00 -0700
Subject: Helios signed amendment received — next internal ops steps

Folks —

Helios signed the amendment this morning (attached: helios_amendment_signed.pdf). They accepted the operator-only fallback language and the dedicated pool terms, with a 90d timebox. Legal accepted the wording but asked us to keep a short audit trail of any manual fallback invocations.

Action items I’m assigning: 
- Hannah: schedule provisioning (target: provision and pre-warm by 2026-06-04). Confirm GPU count and write a short incident playbook for operator-triggered fallback.
- Jonas: add the temporary exception to the product exceptions registry and mark for a post-mortem at 60d.
- Lauren / Karthik: please record the amendment and billing impact in the deal record (deal HHL-2026-0342).

Security has requested a brief network validation; I’ll share Helios’ topology and creds with Security (redacted) — they have a 24-hour SLA to respond.

Thanks all — good win for the team but we need to treat this as a fragile configuration and be deliberate about the rollback story.

—Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
